author: tzjames
body:
### Features and Changes
Allow remote downgrade of licenses and show a message override from the license server.  We need this in case our customers are not paying up.  The override message will be used in the following cases: 		
- They aren't responding to our emails so we're using this to get their attention and tell them to reply to us
- We agreed to some super custom deal terms and the dynamic message language won't make sense

While implementing there were a few cases in the back-end which were relying on accountPlan which didn’t take into account whether there was an error with the license, so I changed that.  We weren't also downgrading due to mismatching orgId - so I centralized the check in a new `getEffectiveAccountPlan` function and made sure `orgHasPremiumFeature` calls it.  There were a few other small cleanups and improvements made.  Here is the full list:

- No longer export planHasPremiumFeature since it is not used externally of license.ts
- Created a new getLicenseErrorMessage function
- Created a new getEffectiveAccountPlan that takes into account if is expired, wrong org or remotely downgraded.
- Removed license middleware.  According to https://github.com/growthbook/growthbook/pull/1006/files#r1110309335 and git grep the header was not used, and git grep says that req.locals.licenseError was only used in one place in organization.controller.ts, so the middleware is no longer needed.
- Changed organization.controller.ts to check the license error directly itself.
- Changed orgHasPremiumFeature to use new getEffectiveAccountPlan for non-cloud.
- Have backend permissions check all use orgHasPremiumFeature instead
- Added new CommercialFeature for scim (it had been directly checking whether the plan was enterprise before)
- Attach effectiveLicensePlan to the userContext.
- If license has a message property use that to construct an AccountPlanNotice.
- Format the date in the expiry tooltip message of AccountPlanNotice
- Got rid of accountPlans as an option in SidebarLink as we weren’t using it in the one place we call SidebarLink: Layout.
- Stopped showing the badge if they no longer have the license features available due to a license error, in order to make it clear that they no longer have enterprise features.
- Refresh the organization when we get new license data as that has the commercial features available and the accountPlan - this allows us to see the Badge disappear without a page refresh.
- Show any AccountPlanNotice in the ShowLicenseInfo to further make it clear when there is an issue.
- Remove an out of date comment in Layout.tsx

### Testing

Insert the following into your shell with the correct authorization bearer and x-organization header taken by looking at a request in dev tools: 
```
postChecklist() {
curl -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_BEARER_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Organization: org_YOUR_ORG_ID" \
  -d '{
    "tasks": [
      {
        "name": "Task 1",
        "completed": false
      },
      {
        "name": "Task 2",
        "completed": true
      }
    ],
    "projectId": "your-project-id"
  }' \
  http://localhost:3100/experiments/launch-checklist
}
```

Add a valid trial enterprise license key to backend/.env.local
Go to Settings->General page.
See the correct license data.
See no account notice
See the badge.
Go to Settings->Logs page
See the export button is enabled.
See that scim works.
run `postChecklist` and see it work.

On the central license server:
Set the license expiry to be in the past
Go to Settings->General page.
Click refresh license.
See the correct license data.
See the expiry account notice
See the badge disappear (when trials end we revert them to free version functionality)
Go to Settings->Logs page
See the export button is disabled and there is a message saying it is only available in enterprise.
See that scim fails.
run `postChecklist` and see it fail.

On the central license server:
Change the license to no longer be a trial.
Go to Settings->General page.
Click refresh license.
See the correct license data.
See the expiry account notice
See the badge re-appear (when enterprise accounts have expired we assume it is an oversight and let them keep full enterprise functionality until we remotely downgrade them.)
Go to Settings->Logs page
See the export button is enabled. 
See that scim works.
run `postChecklist` and see it work.

On the central license server:
click the remotely downgrade button, and confirm (the AccountPlanNotice text is currently hardcoded, the tooltip isn't).
Go to Settings->General page.
Click refresh license.
See the correct license data.
See the hardcoded message, with tooltip.
See the badge disappear (to make clear they no longer have enterprise features).
Go to Settings->Logs page
See the export button is disabled and there is a message saying it is only available in enterprise.
See that scim fails.
run `postChecklist` and see it fail.

author: jods4
body:
`xs:dateTime` can optionally include an offset.

As linqtoxsd generates `DateTime` properties for those, some information is lost during parsing and it's impossible to write xml containing timezone information.

I added one new option, very similar to previously added `DateOnly` support: `<UseDateTimeOffset>`.
When it's true, linqtoxsd generates `DateTimeOffset` properties instead of `DateTime`.
(This is a global settings, there's no pick-and-choose options now.)

It's a rather small change because System.Xml classes already support converting `xs:dateTime` into `DateTimeOffset`, so it mostly "just works".

I added a round-trip test to verify the behavior.

I have issues with some tests failing locally, but I honestly don't think it's related. Do you have known tests failures on `master` right now?

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

- Upgrade `rocksjni` dependency to 8.9.1

### Why are the changes needed?

Due to the performance regression in [JDK 17 attach/detach calls](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8314859), JDK 17 Structured Streaming workloads that stress RocksDB also experience a performance regression. We plan to mitigate this issue by writing RocksDB logs to `stderr` instead of the JVM Log4J logger, as implemented in [this RocksDB PR](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/pull/12213).

However, as that will likely come out in RocksDB 8.10, we'd like to incrementally upgrade to verify that there aren't issues with bumping all the way from 8.3.2 to 8.9.1. 

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

WIP. Likely:

- Benchmark tool for KV store

author: gavinzz
body:
>  Can't destroy a stack that includes a rds database and rds parameter group where the database has removalPolicy property set to RemovalPolicy.RETAIN

### The following is the current behaviour:
```
const parameterGroup = new ParameterGroup(this, 'ParameterGroup', {
    ...
}

const database = new DatabaseInstance(this, 'DatabaseInstance', {
    parameterGroup: parameterGroup,
    removalPolicy: RemovalPolicy.RETAIN,
    ...
})
```

When destroying the stack
```
When I destroy this stack I see the following errors:

2:04:24 PM | DELETE_FAILED        | AWS::RDS::DBParameterGroup                  | ParameterGroup5E32DECB
One or more database instances are still members of this parameter group xxx-database-parametergroup5e32decb-daetrwpaqpgw, so the group cannot be deleted (Service: Rd
s, Status Code: 400, Request ID: 389b18db-ea82-482b-a0e6-f64887da6f82)

2:19:21 PM | DELETE_FAILED        | AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup                     | DatabaseInstanceSecurityGroup8BDF0112
resource sg-0bfc8aacb3d3e3d4a has a dependent object (Service: AmazonEC2; Status Code: 400; Error Code: DependencyViolation; Request ID: 1eac5393-83df-48cf-bd75-41f25abb04
7a; Proxy: null)

```

As pointed out in the issue linked below, we cannot simply use the clusterRds' or instanceRds' removal policy because the parameter group can be simultaneously binded to a cluster and an instance. 

### New behaviour:
Add an optional property `removalPolicy` to the L2 Parameter Group resource and set the deletion policy to the generated L1 Parameter Group (Either cluster or instance) depending on the usage. 

Added unit test and integration test to verify that it works as expected.

Closes https://github.com/aws/aws-cdk/issues/22141
